audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty text treats Mel as a reactive shield-poke laner and never names a single ability; the level chart also disagrees with itself between layers.
audit.why: Annie is 58.32% over 691 games. The real difficulty driver is Solar Snare (E, 1000 range, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s) landing before Annie closes 600 units, plus Overwhelm chip converting into Golden Eclipse damage later.
audit.corrected: Even-to-favoured lane: Annie wins any exchange she starts with a stocked Pyromania stun, and loses the ones Mel opens with Solar Snare at 1000 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text calls Golden Eclipse a channelled beam that must stand still, and tells the player to Flash-stun her mid-cast.
audit.why: Riot's text: Golden Eclipse strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance (range 25000, 120/100/80s). There is no channel and no beam. Advice built on interrupting it is unfollowable.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike for Annie is Flash-Tibbers inside 600 units; Mel's 6 spike is a global cash-out of Overwhelm stacks she has already put on you, so the counterplay is refusing chip, not dodging a cast.
sources: brief enemyKit R text and range

audit.whatIsWrong: No Mel ability is named anywhere; Rebuttal is described as a 'passive reflect shield'; the reflect is treated as always-available.
audit.why: Rebuttal is Mel's W, a 250-range self-barrier on 38/35/33/29/26s that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed. Annie's Q Disintegrate is a projectile (625 range). That is the one interaction that decides whether her poke trade or Annie's costs more, and it is off for roughly thirty seconds at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Bait Rebuttal, then commit into its cooldown; Annie's Q is the projectile it wants, so throw W/auto first when the barrier is glowing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Overwhelm execute threshold, the passive's bonus-projectile auto after every ability cast, and the fact that Annie has no dash out of a Solar Snare are absent.
audit.why: All three come from the missingInteractions list for this exact matchup.
audit.corrected: Track Overwhelm as an HP number, treat Mel casting any ability as a loaded auto, and hold Flash for Solar Snare rather than for damage.

edits.before: Mel wins by landing Rebuttal, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Mel wins by stacking Overwhelm with Radiant Volley chip, then cashing it out with a global Golden Eclipse at range.

edits.before: - Mel Rebuttal: matchup-defining — Reflects your projectiles back — never poke while it glows. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Molten Shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Rebuttal is a 38-second barrier at rank 1 — it reflects your Q, so bait it out, then walk in during the long stretch it is gone. - Solar Snare's root is 11s, her only lockdown. - Your E answers disaster; your R answers the opening.

edits.before: If Mel opens the score, reset expectations and respect Rebuttal doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Mel opens the score, her Overwhelm stacks turn every chip into Golden Eclipse damage — refuse the poke. Farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry by closing distance — Mel has no dash, so Flash-Tibbers lands whenever Rebuttal is spent; engineer that radius.

edits.before: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk he answered with nothing.
edits.after: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk she cannot walk out of.

edits.before: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with his engage loaded — unstacked Annie is the most killable mage in the lane.
edits.after: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with Solar Snare up — unstacked Annie is the most killable mage in this lane.

edits.before: Reflects your projectiles back — never poke while it glows. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Pyromania makes your Q point-and-click, so it lands as she strafes. Unstacked, every commit of yours is a coin flip.

edits.before: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk he answered with nothing.
edits.after: Solar Snare roots and Radiant Volley ticks on top — pop E as her orb flies and step out; the shield eats the burst she set up.

edits.before: That’s Mel’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Three stacks is a Q with no stun — Mel walks out and chips you back.

edits.before: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with his engage loaded — unstacked Annie is the most killable mage in the lane.
edits.after: Mel has no dash to leave Tibbers' burn, and a held ult banks nothing while her Overwhelm stacks keep climbing on you.

edits.before: Mel's reflected-damage shield punishes careless poke, but you can bait it out with W before committing your real all-in combo.
edits.after: Rebuttal reflects your Q and stops her taking damage — bait it with the W cone, then commit the stun combo into its long cooldown.

edits.before: Mel's ultimate beam demands she stand still and channel, giving you a free window to stun and burst her down with Tibbers backup.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse is global and needs no aim — it cashes her Overwhelm stacks, so refuse the chip and Flash-Tibbers her at level 6.

edits.before: A fed Mel's reflect shield and beam ult can delete you in one exchange if she catches you engaging without vision or backup.
edits.after: A fed Mel who has stacked Overwhelm on you can kill from across the map with Golden Eclipse — break contact and stop feeding chip.

edits.before: Annie's Tibbers-backed all-in punishes Mel's committal channel ultimate hard at level 6.
edits.after: Annie's Tibbers-backed all-in kills Mel before Overwhelm stacks reach Golden Eclipse range at 6.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 start tilting your way as your stun uptime and item lead let you force fights on your terms rather than hers — bait, then burst, then follow with Tibbers for the kill. Her ultimate requires a channel, which is a huge liability against a laner who can flash-stun her mid-cast, so punish any premature ult usage hard. By level 6 your Tibbers-backed all-in outclasses her kit as long as you respect the shield mechanic.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 tilt your way as your stun uptime and item lead let you force fights on your terms rather than hers — bait Rebuttal, then burst, then follow with Tibbers. Golden Eclipse is not a cast you can interrupt: it fires globally and scales with the Overwhelm she has already stacked on you, so the counterplay is refusing her chip, not dodging it. By level 6 your Flash-stun all-in outclasses her kit whenever Rebuttal is down.

edits.before: Your first item spike lets you consistently win the skill-testing exchanges since you can now burst through her shield's damage cap in one rotation. However, a fed Mel with full build can reflect a huge chunk of burst back at you and her ultimate beam deletes squishies at range, so a scaled Mel who's ahead in gold can punish a sloppy engage severely — always confirm her shield and ultimate are down before diving in.
edits.after: Your first item spike lets you consistently win the skill-testing exchanges since you can now burst her down in one rotation once the barrier is gone. However, a fed Mel reflects your Q back with Rebuttal and Golden Eclipse cashes stacked Overwhelm at any range, so a scaled Mel ahead in gold punishes a sloppy engage severely — confirm Rebuttal and her ultimate are down before diving in.

edits.before: Poke safely and let her passive reflect shield soak your trades
edits.after: Poke from 950 with Radiant Volley and soak your trades with Rebuttal

edits.before: Use her ultimate's range advantage to punish your approach
edits.after: Chip you with Radiant Volley, then cash Overwhelm with her ult

Repeated factual error killed: Golden Eclipse is not a channelled beam, it is a global (25000 range) strike on Overwhelm-marked enemies, so all 'flash-stun her mid-channel' advice was unfollowable. Rebuttal is Mel's W (38/35/33/29/26s), not a passive.
